page: Hetzner Cloud cpx12 is an entry-tier virtual server operating on the QEMU hypervisor, equipped with 1 shared virtual CPU from an AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. Built upon the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes extended instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, AES, and SHA-NI. The hardware profile provides 2.0 GB of memory and 40 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The instance does not include a dedicated GPU and is provisioned without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark testing reflects the constraints and strengths of a single-core shared resource. In stress-ng single-core compute evaluations, the instance achieved a score of 2999.88, categorizing its single-threaded processing in the top 25 percent. Multi-core stress-ng testing produced the identical score due to the single-core limitation, positioning aggregate processing in the bottom 25 percent alongside a PassMark CPU score of 2673.99. Memory bandwidth performance registers at 146.65 GB/s in cached 16 KB read tests and 28.87 GB/s in uncached 256 MB write tests. Single-threaded data handling tests recorded 24.66 GB/s for gzip compression and 12.27 GB/s for bzip3 decompression.

Application-level throughput aligns with entry-tier hardware allocations, yielding 2.11 GB/s in static web serving benchmarks, 2.79 million operations per second for Redis SET requests, and a PassMark database score of 1004.95. In small model machine learning inference tests, text generation reached 107.47 tokens per second using a 135M parameter model. The shared CPU allocation and low memory capacity establish a cost-efficient hardware balance for low-intensity environments. Hetzner Cloud cpx12 is best suited for lightweight web serving, automation scripts, edge utilities, microservices, and development workloads.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx12 is an entry-tier virtual instance featuring 1 shared AMD EPYC vCPU on the x86_64 architecture clocked at 2.0 GHz, 2.0 GB of system memory, and 40 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The processor incorporates AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates capable single-thread compute with a stress-ng single-core score of 2999.88, placing it in the top 25 percent, while overall multi-core and PassMark CPU metrics reflect the physical single-core limit. Memory operations reach 28.87 GB/s in uncached write tests, supported by 24.66 GB/s single-threaded gzip compression and 2.79 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance omits dedicated GPUs and complimentary IPv4 addresses, providing a resource-dense configuration for lightweight microservices, automation jobs, test pipelines, and low-traffic web applications.
